source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Is there an algorithm to decide whether or not a given subgroup H <Modg is freely indecomposable? Whether or not H splits over Z? 28 B. Farb
technical_scope: Both free indecomposability and splitting over infinite cyclic groups, uniformly in the encoded subgroup of Mod_g.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: A decision procedure needs a finite input model and termination, not enumeration of splittings. The preceding primary question concerns finitely presented subgroups; the target itself does not specify its input encoding. No algorithm established.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: (Morita). Is H1(Kg, Z) finitely generated for g≥ 3? Note that Birman-Craggs-Johnson (see, e.g., [ BC, Jo1 ]) and Morita [ Mo2] have found large abelian quotients of Kg. The proof in [ BF] of Theorem 5.1, suggests an approach to answering to Question 5.2. Let me briefly describe the idea. Following the the outline in [ McM], we first find an action of Kg on the 2. Some problems on mapping class groups and moduli space 37 first homology of a certain abelian cover Y of Σ g; this action respects the structure of H1(Y, Z) as a module over the Galois group of the cover. The crucial piece is that we are able to reduce this to a representation ρ:Kg→ SL2(Z[t,t −1]) on the special linear group over the ring of integral laurent polynomials in one variable. This group acts on an associated Bruhat-Tits-Serre tree, and one can then analyze this action using combinatorial group theory. One might now try to answer Question 5.2 in the negative by systematically computing more elements in the image of ρ, and then analyzing more closely the action on the tree for SL 2. One potentially useful ingredient is a theorem of Grunewald-Mennike-Vaserstein [ GMV] which gives free quotients of arbitrarily high rank for the group SL 2(Z[t]) and the group SL 2(K[s,t ]), where K is an arbitrary finite field. Since we know for g ≥ 3 that Ig is finitely generated and Kg is not, it is natural to ask about the subgroups interpolating between these two. To be precise, consider the exact sequence (11). Corresponding to each subgroup L <∧3H/H is its pullback π−1(L). The lattice of such subgroups L can be thought of as a kind of interpolation between Ig andKg.
technical_scope: Integral H_1(K_g) finite generation for each g>=3.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Infinite generation of a group does not imply infinite generation of its abelianization. The suggested Laurent-polynomial/tree representation needs an actual image/quotient argument. Historical Theorem5.1 is not adopted as a current reliable premise; no new proof or successor audit.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: For which k≥ 1 is it true that Aut(Ig(k)) = Mod ± g? that Comm(Ig(k)) = Mod± g? Theorem 5.17 answers the question for k = 1, 2. It would be remarkable if all of Mod g could be reconstructed from subgroups deeper down in its lower central series.
technical_scope: Determine all k>=1 for both Aut and abstract commensurator of Johnson-filtration terms.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Primary Theorem5.17 covers k=1,2 with genus qualifications nearby; recovering curves from deeper subgroups is a rigidity theorem, not a finite computation. No extrapolation from two terms.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Give an elementary, purely combinatorial-topological and group-theoretic, proof of Hain ’s theorem. It seems that a solution to Problem 5.19 will likely require us to advance our understanding ofIg in new ways. It may also give a hint towards attacking the following problem, where mixed Hodge theory does not apply. 44 B. Farb
technical_scope: Alternative elementary proof of Hain's theorem.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: The requested novelty is a proof method of an already named theorem; no new theorem credit. Exact Hain theorem and genus conditions absent from literal record; no elementary proof produced.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: (Malcev mod 2). Give an explicit finite presentation for the F2-Lie algebra L2(Ig,1). We can also build a Lie algebra using the Johnson filtration. Let hg:= ∞⨁ k=1 Ig(k) Ig(k + 1) ⊗ R Then h is a real Lie algebra. In §14 of [ Ha3], Hain proves that the Johnson filtration is not cofinal with the lower central series of Ig. He also relates hg to tg. The following basic question remains open.
technical_scope: Explicit finite presentation of the mod-2 Lie algebra L_2(I_g,1).
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: A presentation needs all generators, relators, grading and proof of completeness. The record does not define the lower exponent filtration; nearby source definitions must precede any construction. No finite truncation substitutes for it.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Give an algorithm which tells whether or not any given pseudo-Anosov is represented by a simple closed Teichm¨ uller geodesic, and also whether or not this geodesic lies on a Veech curve. Note that the analogue of Question 7.7 is not known for hyperbolic surfaces, although it is true for a generic set of surfaces in Mg. 52 B. Farb
technical_scope: For every pseudo-Anosov, decide both simple closed Teichmueller-geodesic and Veech-curve membership.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Train-track computation alone supplies neither a self-intersection decision nor a Veech-curve criterion with termination. Two independent output obligations; no bounded full-scope route.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Give upper and lower bounds for L(Ig(k)) for all k≥ 2 which are of the same order of magnitude. In [ FLM] bounds on L(H) are given for various special classes of subgroups H < Modg. It seems like there is much more to explore in this direction. One can also combine these types of questions with problems such as Problem 7.5.

definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Needs definition of L and dependence on genus and depth. A finite list of dilatations proves no uniform asymptotic order; no matching mechanism.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Determine the metric completion of the Gromov boundary of C(S) and relate this metric completion to the geometry of C(S). There is yet another way to construct unparametrized uniform quasi-geodesics in C(S). Namely, Teichm¨ uller spaceforS is the space Tg,m of marked isometry classes of complete hyperbolic met- rics on S of finite volume. The Teichm¨ uller space can naturally be identified with a domain in C3g−3+m (see Chapter 6 of [IT]). By a classical result of Bers (see [Bu]), there is a number χ> 0 such that for every complete hyperbolic metric h on S there is a pants decomposition for S consisting of simple closed h- geodesics of length at most χ. Moreover, the diameter in C(S) of the set of simple closed curves on S of h-length at most χ is bounded from above by a universal constant D >0. Thus we can define a map Ψ: Tg,m→C (S) by associating to a marked hyperbolic metric h a simple closed curve of h-length at most χ. For any two such maps Ψ, Ψ′ we then have sup h∈Tg,md(Ψ(h), Ψ′(h))≤D. The Teichm¨ uller metriconTg,m is a complete Finsler metric which is just the Kobayashi metric on the domain in C3g−3+m representingTg,m (see [IT]). Through any two distinct points in Tg,m passes a unique Teichm¨ uller geodesic. Each such geodesic line in Tg,m is uniquely determined by its endpoints in the Thurston boundary ofTg,m which is just the space PML of projective measured laminations on S. The supports of the two measured laminations on S defining the endpoints of the geodesic together fill up the surface S, i.e. every simple closed curve on S intersects at least one of the two laminations transversely. These laminations then define a holomorphic quadratic 14. Geometric properties of the mapping class group 235 diﬀerential (we refer to Section 4 of [Ke] for a discussion of this fact). The following result is implicitly contained in the paper [MM1] by Masur and Minsky; an explicit proof using a result of Rafi [R] can be found in Section 4 of [H4].
technical_scope: Metric completion of curve-complex Gromov boundary related to C(S).
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Visual metrics depend on choices and snowflaking; completeness cannot be inferred from the boundary's topological identification alone. Need the intended metric before a completion theorem.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Develop a theory of geometrically finite subgroups of Mg,m which include the groups defined by Veech surfaces. 14. Geometric properties of the mapping class group 241
technical_scope: A geometric-finiteness theory including Veech-surface groups.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: This is a framework request, not a fixed yes/no proposition. Convex cocompactness alone need not include cusp/parabolic behavior of Veech groups. No full-scope mechanism.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Is the mapping class group a-T-menable? 14. Geometric properties of the mapping class group 245
technical_scope: Haagerup/a-T-menability of the mapping class group.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Requires proper affine isometric Hilbert action or an actual obstruction. An action on a curve graph does not supply such an action; low genus cases are insufficient.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: (Ergodic measures). Classify the ergodic measures for the action of SL(2, R) on H1(α) andQ1(β). McMullen [ McM3] has solved Problems 9 and 10 in the case of translation surfaces in genus 2. A subset Ω is called minimal for the action of SL(2, R) if it is closed, invariant, and it has no proper closed invariant subsets. The SL(2, R) orbit of a Veech surface is an example of a minimal set.
technical_scope: Classify all ergodic SL(2,R)-invariant measures in abelian and quadratic unit-area strata.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Primary gives genus2 as already treated. Measure-rigidity successors are essential before any investment, including finite covers for quadratic differentials; no new classification and no successor body read.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: (Lyapunov exponents). Study individual Lyapunov exponents of the Teichm¨ uller geodesic flow: – for all known SL(2; R)-invariant subvarieties; – for strata; – for strata of large genera as the genus tends to infinity. Are they related to characteristic numbers of any natural bundles over appropriate compacti- fications of the strata? The motivation for this problem is a beautiful formula of Kontsevich [ Ko] representing the sum of the first g Lyapunov exponents in diﬀerential-geometric terms. It follows from the Calabi Theorem [ Cb] that given a real closed 1-form ω0 with isolated zeroes Σ (satisfying some natural conditions) on a smooth surface S of real dimension two, one 15. Problems on billiards, flat surfaces and translation surfaces 255 can find a complex structure on S and a holomorphic 1-form ω such that the ω0 is the real part of ω. Consider the resulting point ( X,ω ) in the corresponding stratum. For generic ( X,ω ) the cocycle related to the Teichm¨ uller geodesic flow acting on H 1(X, R) defines a pair of transverse Lagrangian subspaces H 1(X, R) = L0⊕L1 by means of the Oseledets Theorem ([ BaPe]). These subspaces correspond to contracting and to expanding directions. Though the pair ( X,ω ) is not uniquely determined by ω0, the subspace L0⊂H 1(X, R) does not depend on ( X,ω ) for a given ω0. Moreover, L0 does not change under small deformations of ω0 that preserve the cohomology class [ ω]∈H 1(S, Σ; R). We get a topological object L0 defined in implicit dynamical terms.
technical_scope: Individual Lyapunov exponents on all known invariant subvarieties, strata, and large-genus limits, with characteristic-number relationship.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Kontsevich's sum formula does not determine individual exponents. Several independent asymptotic/geometric obligations, no finite certificate for the full program.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Is every finite rank subgroup of Whittlesey’s group a Schottky subgroup of MCG (S)? As a consequence of Theorem 2.1, if H <MCG (S) has a finite index subgroup which is Schottky, that is, if H is a virtual Schottky subgroup, then Γ H has a finite index word hyperbolic subgroup and so Γ H is itself word hyperbolic.
technical_scope: Every finite-rank subgroup of Whittlesey's group is Schottky.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Pure pseudo-Anosov behavior does not itself give a quasi-isometric orbit/convex-cocompactness proof. Need exact surface and finite-rank convention; no general mechanism.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: LetH be a surface subgroup of Γg. Is Γg H-separable? For recent progress on various classes of subgroups of Γ g that are separable, we refer the reader to [ 24].
technical_scope: Every surface subgroup H of Gamma_g is separable.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Separating each outside element by a finite quotient requires a general quotient construction. Residual finiteness of the ambient group alone does not imply subgroup separability.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: Does there exist a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold that is a surface bundle over a surface where the genus of the fiber and base is 2? 4.2. Some evidence for a negative answer to Question 4.1 is given in [ 21] where the following conjecture is stated (this is a special case of a more general conjecture on vanishing of Seiberg- Witten invariants). We refer to [ 37] and [ 14] for definitions.
technical_scope: A closed real-hyperbolic4 manifold fibering with both fiber and base genus2.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Euler characteristic would be16 by multiplicativity, but that necessary integer condition neither constructs nor obstructs a hyperbolic metric. No full existence or nonexistence argument.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

If such an injection exists does there exist a continuous Γ-equivariant map ∂∞(Γ)→ PML0(Σ)? More generally, for a fixed Σ and hence fixed vcd, a further natural generalization of the discussion here is: 284 A.W. Reid
technical_scope: For all admissible lattices in specified SO/SU families, injections, purely pseudo-Anosov representations and equivariant boundary maps.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Admissibility and PML_0 missing; three different existence/extension questions. Superrigidity analogy is not an exact obstruction theorem under these hypotheses.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

technical_scope: Describe iwip axis-bundle geometry in Outer space.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Definitions of axis bundle and associated objects are omitted; contractibility or uniqueness would be distinct endpoints. No rigorous bounded classification extracted.

source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics
statement: If there is a homomorphism from a subgroup of finite index in Aut(Fn) onto a subgroup of finite index in GL(m, Z), then must m≥n− 1? 324 M. Bridson and K. Vogtmann Indeed one might ask:

The following primary Question2.7 explicitly concerns finite image, explaining intended nontrivial scope. This endpoint loophole earns no credit.

Perhaps the most promising approach to Question 17 is via bounded cohomology, following the template of Bestvina and Fujiwara’s work on subgroups of the mapping class group [ 6].
technical_scope: Random-walk theory on Outer space analogous to Kaimanovich-Masur.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Needs random-walk measure hypotheses and a concrete convergence/boundary endpoint. Bounded-cohomology method similarity is not a solution or routine-subsumption bridge; successor bodies unread.

technical_scope: Nonzero image of second Morita class in rational H_8(GL(6,Z)).

Also compare these classes with the homology classes constructed by Conant and Vogtmann [10] as explicit cycles in the moduli space of graphs. Furthermore investigate whether these classes survive in H∗(GL(n, Z); Q), or else come fromH∗(IOutn; Q), or not.

Morita Acknowledgments The author would like to express his hearty thanks to R. Hain, N. Kawazumi, D. Kotschick, M. Matsumoto, H. Nakamura, T. Sakasai for enlightening discussions as well as useful informations concerning the problems treated in this paper.

technical_scope: Existence of theta_6 in pi_126^S, equivalently permanence of h_6 squared.

source_name: Hovey's Algebraic Topology Problem List (proposed by Mark Hovey)

Cohen - Goerss result proving that h_0 h_i is a permanent cycle in the Adams spectral sequence for all primes bigger than 3 is wrong. The flaw was found by Minami, and it appears to be fatal to their proof. So this problem is still open.

definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Exact indexing and spectral-sequence conventions needed. The record reports a fatal flaw in the classical proof; neither repeating it nor verifying a finite range supplies the all-primes family.

source_name: Hovey's Algebraic Topology Problem List (proposed by Mark Hovey)
statement: Classify the localizing subcategories of the stable k[G]-module category. These should be in 1-1 correspondence with arbitrary subsets of Proj H^*(G,k). I have no idea how to do this one.
technical_scope: Classify all localizing subcategories of stable k[G]-modules by arbitrary subsets of Proj H*(G,k).
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Finiteness of G, characteristic and module-category conventions are omitted. Support-theory classification is a substantial known-literature lead needing theorem-body comparison; no claimed new classification.

source_name: Topology problems from Wikipedia (proposed by Barry Mazur)
statement: For every algebraic variety $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, does the closure of $X(\mathbb{Q})$ inside the real locus $X(\mathbb{R})$ have only finitely many connected components?
technical_scope: Every Q-variety has finitely many components in the closure of its rational points in X(R).
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Semialgebraic finiteness of X(R) does not imply finiteness for the closure of X(Q). Need arithmetic control of that subset; no uniform mechanism.

source_name: arXiv
statement: For every synchronizing deterministic finite automaton $\mathcal{A}=(Q,\Sigma,\delta)$ with $|Q|=n$, there exists a word $w\in\Sigma^*$ and a state $q_0\in Q$ such that $\delta(q,w)=q_0$ for every $q\in Q$ and $|w|\leq (n-1)^2$.
technical_scope: Every synchronizing n-state deterministic automaton has a reset word of length <=(n-1)^2.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Finite search for a chosen n is only a parameter test. A full improvement from cubic general bounds to quadratic requires a global compression mechanism; none supplied.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/01, page 48
statement:
Are any two simple Ramsey systems consistent? Equivalently, for fixed positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$, does every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admit sequences $(x_i)_{i\ge 1}$ and $(y_i)_{i\ge 1}$ such that
$$\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_jx_{i_j}:i_1<\cdots<i_m\right\}\cup\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{n}b_jy_{i_j}:i_1<\cdots<i_n\right\}$$
is monochromatic?
technical_scope: Consistency of any two simple positive-coefficient Ramsey systems.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Source pp52-53 explicitly reports this proved by Hindman-Leader-Strauss and a shorter Leader-Russell proof. Read definitions and resolution passage, not their entire proof bodies. Do not confuse inconsistent Milliken-Taylor systems with these simple systems.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/01, page 54
statement:
Let \(L\) be the length of the longest common subsequence of two uniformly and independently chosen words of length \(n\) over an alphabet of size \(k\), and let \(\gamma_k=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[L]/n\). The conjecture is
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\gamma_k\sqrt{k}=2.
\]
technical_scope: lim_{k->infty} gamma_k sqrt(k)=2 with independent uniform length-n words.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Source Theorem1 pp59-60 bounds E[L] between (1+-epsilon)2n/sqrt(k) for all large k and n/sqrt(k)>C, which implies the target by n->infty then k->infty. Read theorem and block/LIS proof outline; full-paper concentration dependencies not audited.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/01, page 67
statement:
For every even integer $k\ge 4$, and also for $k=3$, there exist $k$-graphs $F$ and $H$ such that
$$\pi(\{F,H\})<\min\{\pi(F),\pi(H)\}.$$
technical_scope: For each even k>=4 and k=3, a non-principal pair of k-graphs.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Source p71 Theorem2 is exactly the assertion and includes its stability construction: stable F, cone H of a large clique, and Lemma1 edge-removal contradiction. Read complete local proof; invoked stability theorems not replayed. Odd k>=5 is outside the target.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/01, page 100
statement: The kissing number in dimension four is $\kappa(4)=24$.
technical_scope: kappa(4)=24.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Source pp103-104 discusses Musin's announced proof and optimization mechanism. This is strong prior evidence, not a replay of the exact nonconvex optimization certificate. No new result or full proof-body audit claimed.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/05, page 30
statement:
For the Nekrasov equation
\[
\theta(\sigma)=\frac{1}{3\pi}\int_0^\pi \log\left\lvert\frac{\sin\frac{\sigma+s}{2}}{\sin\frac{\sigma-s}{2}}\right\rvert\,\frac{\mu\sin\theta(s)}{1+\mu\int_0^s\sin\theta(u)\,du}\,ds,\qquad 0<\sigma\leq\pi,
\]
does there exist at most one non-trivial solution satisfying \(0\leq\theta(\sigma)\leq\pi\) for \(0\leq\sigma\leq\pi\), for every \(\mu\in(3,\infty)\)?
technical_scope: At most one nontrivial constrained Nekrasov solution for every mu>3.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: The nonlinear denominator couples all earlier s. A naive contraction is not uniform for large mu, and local bifurcation uniqueness does not imply global uniqueness. No monotonicity/comparison theorem established.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/05, page 41
statement:
For the generalized Benjamin–Ono equation
\[
\partial_t u+H\partial_x^2u\pm u^k\partial_xu=0,\qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R,\qquad u(0,x)=u_0(x),
\]
where \(H\) is the Hilbert transform and \(k\ge 2\) is an integer, establish a well-posedness result in the energy space \(H^{1/2}(\mathbb R)\) for arbitrary large initial data.
technical_scope: Large-data H^(1/2)(R) well-posedness for both signs and every integer k>=2.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Energy control is not a contraction estimate or uniqueness proof. Need precise local/global lifespan endpoint; scaling and endpoint multilinear estimates cannot be replaced by small-data or k-fixed cases.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/07, page 39
statement:
Is it true that every transcendental entire function $f$ of order less than $1/2$ satisfies the following condition? There exist positive numbers $R_0,L,\delta,C$ with $R_0>e$, $M(R_0,f)>e$, $L>1$, and $0<\delta\le 1$ such that, for every $r>R_0$, there exists $t\in(r,r^L]$ for which
\[
\frac{\log m(t,f)}{\log M(r,f)}\ge L\left(1-\frac{C}{(\log r)^\delta}\right).
\]
technical_scope: Every entire transcendental f of order<1/2 admits constants R0,L,delta,C and a good t for every r>R0.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Minimum-modulus results on many radii do not automatically give the stated logarithmic-rate control in every multiplicative interval. No uniform quantitative bridge.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/07, page 49
statement:
If $X$ comes from a subdivision rule with associated expanding map $f$, then
\[
\dim_{AR} X=\inf\{Q\ge 2:\lambda(f,\Gamma,Q)<1\text{ for all $f$-stable multicurves }\Gamma\}.
\]
Moreover, $\dim_{AR}X$ is never attained unless $X\mathrel{\simeq_{qs}}S^2$.
technical_scope: Exact AR conformal dimension spectral-radius infimum for all f-stable multicurves, plus nonattainment unless qs sphere.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Need subdivision/expansion hypotheses and lambda definition. Lower bounds from obstructions alone do not prove upper realization or nonattainment. No full route.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/10, page 3
statement: Every finite subset of a Gabor frame is linearly independent.
technical_scope: Every finite subset of every Gabor frame is linearly independent.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: The window and lattice conventions matter. Gram positivity for finitely many examples proves no all-frame theorem; this is an HRT-type independence barrier, not a finite matrix exercise.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/10, page 43
statement: Study the Besov spaces introduced in [2] using the theory of co-orbit spaces and the discrete wavelet transform, using the results from [22, 23] applied to the group $GL(C)$.
technical_scope: Coorbit/discrete wavelet study of Besov spaces on symmetric cones via GL(C).
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Spaces, cone, admissibility, norms and references2,22,23 are missing. A generic coorbit theorem cannot be applied without verifying representation and kernel hypotheses.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/12, page 34
statement: Let $G$ be a connected and simply connected compact Lie group. Let $f$ be a virtual character of $G$ such that: (a) $f(x)$ is real and $f(x)\ge 0$ for every $x\in G$; and (b) its mean value satisfies $\langle f,1\rangle=1$. Is it true that $f=\overline{\chi}\chi$ for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$?
technical_scope: For every connected simply connected compact Lie group, nonnegative mean1 virtual characters are irreducible absolute squares.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Primary p666 Question has exactly these hypotheses. Its Theorem2 already answers yes for SU2; rank1 polynomial experiments would duplicate that theorem. Higher rank needs a new positivity/factorization mechanism; no successor body or complete proof.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/13, page 14
statement: For coprime bases $q_1,\ldots,q_d$ and irrational numbers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$, the sequence $\bigl(s_{q_1}(n)\alpha_1,\ldots,s_{q_d}(n)\alpha_d\bigr)_{n\ge 0}$ is uniformly distributed modulo $1$.
technical_scope: Joint distribution of digit sums for coprime bases and arbitrary irrational coefficients.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Primary p685 lists precisely this topic in a survey of recent results, not explicitly as an open conjecture. One-base Fourier factorization does not establish joint decorrelation for different bases. No resolution or novelty inferred from the survey list.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/13, page 25
statement:
Does there exist an algorithm running in time polynomial in $n$ and $d$ that, for every $n,d\in\mathbb N$, constructs a set $M_n\subset[0,1]^d$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{disc}_\infty(M_n)\le c\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}},
\]
where $c>0$ is the constant in Theorem 1, or satisfying a specified slightly weaker estimate?
technical_scope: Uniform polynomial time in both n and d for the stated star-discrepancy bound or a specified weakening.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Source pp697-698 gives probabilistic existence and a moment formula; computing that formula by enumerating n^p terms is not polynomial when p grows with d. Derandomization and bit precision remain substantive, and unspecified weaker estimates cannot be silently chosen.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/13, page 29
statement:
Does there exist a digital $(0,1)$-sequence over $
\mathbb{Z}_2$ generated by an NUT matrix $C$ such that, for some constant $c_1>0$, its $L_2$-discrepancy satisfies
\[
L_{2,N}\le c_1\frac{\sqrt{\log N}}{N}
\]
for every $N\ge 2$?
technical_scope: One fixed binary NUT matrix with L2_N<=c sqrt(log N)/N for every N>=2.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: Primary pp699-702 defines the sequence and discrepancy, then Theorems5-6 show the all-ones-upper-triangular candidate succeeds on density1 scales but fails on infinitely many scales by log(N)/N. A density1 theorem cannot satisfy the universal N quantifier. No other fixed matrix mechanism.

source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/21, page 5
statement: Conjecture: For every projective manifold $X$ that is not uniruled, $\ba^+(X)=\ba(X)$, where $\ba^+(X)$ denotes the modified Kodaira dimension introduced in the report.
technical_scope: For every non-uniruled projective manifold, equality of modified and ordinary Kodaira dimension.
definition_and_mechanism_assessment: The record's ba notation needs source definition before comparison with kappa. Abundance-like implications require complete birational-geometric dependencies; no short full-scope route.
